study_type_evidence.quote: we administered 21 to mice (BALB/c, n = 3) via intraperitoneal (ip) injection at a dose of 20 mg/kg
the testing method involved incubating human plasma with a peptide and then determining the level of pre-beta HDL in the sample by using an ELISA assay
Efflux was measured from mouse macrophage J774 cells incubated with 2% apoB-depleted plasma samples for 4 h.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male BALB/c (HDL remodeling and pharmacokinetic studies); age not reported. BALB/c also used for the LPS inflammation model, sex not stated there
in_vivo_species.quote: Peptide 21 increased the level of pre-beta HDLs after intraperitoneal injection (20 mg/kg) to male BALB/c mice (n = 3), as determined by Western blotting for mouse apoA-I.

ex_vivo_detail: Human plasma was incubated with each cyclic peptide in vitro for 1 h and the resulting pre-beta HDL levels were measured by ELISA and confirmed by Western blot for human apoA-I; this is plasma removed from the body and then treated, so it is classified as ex vivo rather than in vitro. Mouse plasma was also remodeled (the abstract-independent body states remodeling of plasma HDL and Figure 6a shows Western blotting for mouse apoA-I in plasma from dosed mice). Peptide-treated plasma was subsequently apoB-depleted and used as the cholesterol acceptor in the efflux assay. Hemolysis HD50 values were determined on erythrocytes (species not stated).
in_vitro_detail: Cholesterol efflux from cholesterol-laden mouse macrophage J774 cells incubated with 2% apoB-depleted plasma for 4 h; cytotoxicity LD50 against NCI, MCF7 and SKOV-3 cell lines (Table 1); liposome clearance and FPLC assays showing the cyclic peptides do not form peptide-lipid nanoparticles.

agents.name: Peptide 21, c[wLwReQeR]
agents.sequence: wLwReQeR (cyclic d,l-alpha-peptide; capital letters are l-amino acids and small letters are d-amino acids)
agents.sequence_source: Table 1 'Bioactivity and Physical Data for Lead Peptides Identified by HDL Remodeling ELISA' lists no. 21 with sequence wLwReQeR; the Figure 3 legend states 'Capital letters represent l-amino acids; small letters represent d-amino acids.'
agents.chemical_identifier: Theoretical pI 6.14; pre-beta HDL generated 81 ± 11 ug/mL; cytotoxicity LD50 36 uM (NCI), >40 uM (MCF7), >40 uM (SKOV-3); hemolysis HD50 >660 uM (4% at the highest concentration tested)
agents.group_n: n = 3 for both the HDL remodeling and the pharmacokinetic studies; n = 5 per group for the LPS inflammation study
agents.group_n_quote: this rather long period of action in vivo was supported by a pharmacokinetic study for 21 in mice (BALB/c, n = 3)
agents.dose: 20 mg/kg for the HDL remodeling study and 7.5 mg/kg for the anti-inflammatory study; the dose used for the pharmacokinetic study is not separately stated
agents.dose_route_quote: we administered 21 to mice (BALB/c, n = 3) via intraperitoneal (ip) injection at a dose of 20 mg/kg
agents.pk_quote: After ip administration, the peptide had a plasma half-life of approximately 6 h (Figure 6b and Figure S5), consistent with the high proteolytic stability of cyclic d,l-alpha-peptides.
agents.notes_agent: The body also reports a pharmacodynamic duration: 'The effects persisted for up to 8 h from the preinjection time point.' This is a duration of HDL remodeling effect, not a PK parameter.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: The pharmacokinetic half-life of the peptide in vivo was several hours in mice.
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure 6b is cited in the Results as the source of the approximately 6 h plasma half-life for peptide 21 after intraperitoneal dosing, so it plots plasma level against time; the axis units and matrix labelling are not described in the body text.

bioanalytical_quote: No assay for quantifying peptide 21 in plasma is described in the body; the pharmacokinetic result is reported only as 'After ip administration, the peptide had a plasma half-life of approximately 6 h (Figure 6b and Figure S5)'.
notes: The supplied full-text file contains no METHODS or Experimental Section, so the bioanalytical assay, the exact PK dose and the PK sampling schedule are not recoverable from the body. The PEPLIFE2 header lists the assay as LC-MS/SIM; that is database metadata and was not used, so bioanalytical_method is recorded as not reported. The only PK datum in the body is the approximately 6 h plasma half-life of peptide 21 after intraperitoneal dosing. No phase is named, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and half_life_elimination is left as not reported rather than inferred. Dosing was intraperitoneal, so an absorption phase exists, but no absorption half-life and no rate constant is reported and nothing was converted. No Cmax, tmax or AUC is reported. The dose used specifically for the PK study is not stated; 20 mg/kg ip is the dose given for the HDL remodeling experiment in the immediately preceding sentence and 7.5 mg/kg ip was used for the anti-inflammatory study, so the PK dose is recorded as not separately stated. The eight-hour persistence of the pre-beta HDL effect is a pharmacodynamic duration, not a half-life. Over 80 cyclic d,l-alpha-peptides were screened (81 sequences per the Results text, with 73 eight-residue and 8 six-residue peptides); only the sequences printed in the body text or in Table 1 are captured as agent objects, and the remainder are listed only in Table S1, which is not part of the supplied body. Peptides 1, 15, 18, 23-26, 33, 34, 36-39, 41-50 and 52-54 are discussed by number in the Results without their sequences being printed. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), given intraperitoneally to induce the acute inflammation model, is a model-induction agent and is noted here rather than listed as an agent object.
